name: Throw
description:
A mandible spun off the hand. It shared the spit's chirp until now, and a blade going out does not chirp: what you hear of something thrown is the air it cuts, rising as it comes past and dropping as it goes.

`flick` is the release, ten milliseconds of noise under a lowpass — the hand letting go, felt more than heard. `cut` is the flight: noise through a `band` Q whose centre climbs from `$shell.up` to above `$grit` and falls back, under a gain that swells in and fades out, so it reads as a pass rather than a burst. The Q is narrower than the whoosh's because a blade edge whistles a little where smoke does not; it is not `sharp`, because then it would whistle and nothing else. Nothing is pitched — the blade is the air.

The Dancing Mandibles fire a volley of these at once, so three takes and a little jitter keep five of them from landing as one sound five times as loud.
